# opencode-flowgraph [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) **Turn your multi-agent process into a workflow you can run again.** Define your development loop once — plan, build, review, secure, ship — as a YAML graph. Run it with the OpenCode agents you already have. Every run is durable, inspectable, and steerable from the TUI or Desktop. ## What you get - **Your process, not ad-hoc prompts.** Write the review loop once and run it against every change. Same agents, same gates, same outcomes. - **Your agents, not a new runtime.** Workflow nodes use native OpenCode agents from `.opencode/agents`. No hosted backend, no custom LLM client, no second tool to learn. - **Real quality loops.** Agents report structured outcomes; the graph routes on them. `changes_requested` sends work back; `approved` moves it forward; `blocked` pauses for a human. - **Runs that survive interruptions.** Checkpoints are persisted after every transition. Restart the server and completed work is not redone; ambiguous work is blocked, never silently re-run. - **Parallel and reusable workflows.** Fork into concurrent branches, join their results, and call another workflow by name. Start multiple runs in the same checkout. - **Visibility and control.** Follow active steps in the TUI or Desktop graph, open their sessions, and pause, resume, or cancel a run. - **Local-first by default.** Workflows and runtime state stay on your machine. Nothing is sent to a third-party service. - **Guardrails that respect you.** Native permissions still apply. The plugin never auto-approves, never edits your agents, and blocks workflow edits to your OpenCode configuration. ## How it works You bring two things: 1. **Agents** — native Markdown agents in `.opencode/agents/*.md`, owned by OpenCode. 2. **A workflow** — a YAML graph in `.opencode/workflows/*.yaml`, owned by this plugin. The plugin validates the graph, then runs one agent at a time in a fresh OpenCode session. Each agent does its job and reports an outcome. The validated graph — not the agent — decides where the run goes next. State is checkpointed after every step, so runs can pause and recover without losing completed work. ## Onboarding ### 1. Install the plugin Add it to `opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph"] } ``` Pin a version when reproducibility matters: ```jsonc { "plugins": ["@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph@0.8.2"] } ``` OpenCode loads the published package directly. No clone or build required. ### 2. Define an agent Create `.opencode/agents/reviewer.md`. It must be a primary (or `all`) agent with a model and tool access: ```md --- description: Reviews changes for correctness and missing tests mode: primary model: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash --- Review the change. Report findings in severity order. ``` ### 3. Define a workflow Create `.opencode/workflows/development.yaml`: ```yaml version: 1 name: development description: Development with iterative quality checks entry: developer limits: max_steps: 12 timeout_seconds: 3600 nodes: developer: agent: developer next: reviewer reviewer: agent: reviewer routes: approved: complete changes_requested: developer blocked: pause ``` The file stem must match `name`. Every node must be reachable from `entry`, and each node defines either `next` or `routes`. See the [workflow guide](docs/guide.md) for the full schema and limits. ### 4. Run it In the TUI: ```text /flowgraph run development "Add retry handling to the API client" ``` Or open the palette and choose **Flowgraph** to browse runs and workflows. In OpenCode Desktop, use the **Flowgraph** command to pick a run; the experimental GUI panel renders its graph. ### 5. Watch and steer - **TUI** — `/flowgraph` opens the live graph. Use `enter` for the primary active session, `s` to pick a session, and `p` to pause or resume. - **Desktop** — the **Workflow** command opens a run picker; click nodes to inspect their sessions. - **RPC** — `getRun`, `getRunGraph`, `pauseRun`, `resumeRun`, `cancelRun`, and the `runUpdated` event. ## Before you start - OpenCode V2 with `@opencode/plugin` versions `>=2.0.32 <3`. - Agents must be visible, `mode: primary` or `mode: all`, have a model, and be able to use tools. - `mode: subagent` agents are not supported directly. Change them to `mode: all` if you want them in a workflow. - The plugin registers `flowgraph_report`, the typed tool agents use to report outcomes. You do not add it yourself. ## Honest limits - Parallel branches and concurrent runs share the checkout. Overlapping file writes can conflict. - Execution supports one OpenCode server per project database. - No hosted execution, marketplace, visual editor, or browser UI. - Exactly-once external side effects are not promised. Cost is reported, not capped. - The Desktop GUI is experimental; the TUI and RPC are the stable surfaces. ## Ready-made examples [`examples/.opencode`](examples/.opencode) contains agents and four workflows you can copy and adapt, including `parallel-review` for forks, joins, and calls. ## Documentation | Read this | For | |---|---| | [Workflow guide](docs/guide.md) | Agents, YAML schema, routing, outcomes, limits, examples | | [Operations](docs/operations.md) | Execution, recovery, storage, concurrency, permissions, guardrails | | [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) | RPC, `/flowgraph` command, TUI, Desktop GUI, Mermaid | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Architecture, local development, migration, releasing | ## License Apache-2.0. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

# Development

## Architecture and ownership

- OpenCode owns agents, sessions, permissions, models, and tools.
- The plugin owns workflow YAML parsing, graph validation, orchestration, run state, recovery, and Mermaid generation.
- Workflow definitions stay in `.opencode/workflows`.
- Runtime state stays in OpenCode plugin storage, keyed by project.

### Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `workflow/schema.ts` | Zod YAML schema and hard limits |
| `workflow/loader.ts` | Safe YAML parsing, discovery, hashing, atomic file operations |
| `workflow/graph.ts` | Pure graph construction, validation, transition resolution |
| `workflow/mermaid.ts` | Pure, escaped, deterministic Mermaid generation |
| `workflow/validator.ts` | Semantic validation and native agent resolution |
| `execution/native-agents.ts` | Typed adapter over OpenCode agents, sessions, and permissions |
| `execution/report-tool.ts` | `flowgraph_report` tool and active-session registry |
| `execution/tool-hooks.ts` | Workflow-session background-work policy and protected configuration guard |
| `execution/prompts.ts` | Bounded context handoff prompts |
| `execution/results.ts` | Result/audit summarization and usage estimates |
| `execution/run-graph.ts` | Structured run graph, active-node state, session mapping, controls |
| `ui/runs.ts` | Cross-project/worktree run discovery, merge, and ordering |
| `ui/graph.ts` | Pure boxed terminal diagram: ranking, rails, tones, width/height fallback |
| `tui.tsx` | TUI workflow page, session panel, command, keyboard controls |
| `gui.tsx` | Experimental Desktop GUI run picker, panel, and Mermaid renderer |
| `execution/runner.ts` | Concurrent session scheduler, controls, limits, and recovery |
| `execution/checkpoint.ts` | Durable branch, call, and join transitions |
| `state/store.ts` | Project-scoped records with revisioned run mutations |
| `state/concurrency.ts` | Host-local run ownership lock |
| `service.ts` | Workflow discovery/validation and run control facade |
| `rpc.ts` | Shared `Rpc.define` contract |
| `contract.ts` | Shared Zod schemas and exported types |
| `rpc/handlers.ts` | Thin RPC handlers and error mapping |
| `index.ts` | Plugin setup, tool/RPC registration, recovery scheduling, cleanup |

### Structured result boundary

V2 agent prompts do not have a native response schema. The plugin uses a typed tool whose input is validated by OpenCode and persisted by the plugin. Free-form phrases such as `DONE` or `LGTM` are never parsed.

The tool is location-wide because OpenCode plugin tools are not session-scoped. Executors reject calls outside an active workflow node session, and background `subagent`/`shell` calls are rejected inside workflow sessions by default.

## Local development

```sh
bun install
bun run typecheck
bun run test
```

The optional real OpenCode plugin-loading/RPC smoke test:

```sh
OPENCODE_SMOKE=1 OPENCODE_BIN=/path/to/opencode bun run test:smoke
```

It starts an isolated `opencode api --standalone` request, loads the plugin from this repository, and calls `capabilities` and `listWorkflows`. It does not make model calls.

The opt-in model-routing integration uses a local OpenAI-compatible mock server and makes no paid model calls:

```sh
OPENCODE_MODEL_INTEGRATION=1 OPENCODE_BIN=/path/to/opencode bun run test:integration
```

It checks the model IDs and variant sent in actual inference requests. The default unit suite still uses `FakeNative` and does not require an OpenCode binary.

A real-model end-to-end verification is manual: define two primary agents, create the workflow, start a run through RPC, verify the review loop, disconnect the client, restart the server, and confirm conservative recovery. See [`operations.md`](operations.md) and [`interfaces.md`](interfaces.md).

A local plugin entry needs a root `index.ts` (server) and `rpc.ts` (shared contract); this repository provides both.

## Migrating from 0.1.x

Version `0.2.1` is a full rename:

- npm package: `opencode-agent-workflows` → `opencode-flowgraph`
- plugin ID: `agent-workflows` → `flowgraph`
- RPC ID: `agent_workflows` → `flowgraph`
- reporting tool: `agent_workflows_report` → `flowgraph_report`

Update the plugin entry in `opencode.json(c)` and any agent prompts that call the reporting tool. Runs stored under the old plugin ID are not visible to `0.2.1`; start new runs.

## Releasing

Releases are published to the public npm registry from GitHub Actions using npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC). There is no long-lived npm token in the repository.

### Prerequisites

- Public GitHub repository
- npm CLI **11.5.1+**
- Node **22.14+**
- npm account with 2FA enabled

The release workflow installs the latest npm before publishing.

### First publish (one-time bootstrap)

Trusted publishing can only be configured after the package exists on npm. Bootstrap the first version once:

```sh
# From the repository root
npm login
npm publish --access public
```

`npm publish` runs `prepublishOnly`, which typechecks and tests the package.

Then configure the trusted publisher:

1. Open `https://www.npmjs.com/package/@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph`
2. Open **Settings** and find **Trusted Publisher**
3. Choose **GitHub Actions**
4. Enter:
   - **Organization or user:** `alvarolorentedev`
   - **Repository:** `opencode-flowgraph`
   - **Workflow filename:** `release.yml`
   - **Environment name:** leave blank
   - **Allowed actions:** enable **Allow npm publish**
5. Save.

After the configuration is saved, it must complete its first successful publish within 2 days. If it expires, delete it, recreate it, and publish again.

You can also configure it with npm CLI 11.15+:

```sh
npm trust github @alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph \
  --repo alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph \
  --file release.yml \
  --allow-publish
```

Verify:

```sh
npm trust list @alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph
```

After the trusted publisher works, optionally restrict token publishing:

- Package Settings → Publishing access
- Select **Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens**

Do not add an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. The release workflow intentionally has no token fallback.

If you cannot publish locally, use a one-time granular token in a temporary workflow for the bootstrap publish only, then revoke it, remove the secret, and configure trusted publishing.

#### Validate trusted publishing with the next version

A new trusted-publisher configuration must complete a successful OIDC publish within **2 days**. The manual bootstrap version does not validate it.

After configuring the trusted publisher, publish the next patch through GitHub Actions:

```sh
npm version patch --no-git-tag-version
git add package.json bun.lock
git commit -m "release: v0.2.2"
git push

git tag v0.2.2
git push origin v0.2.2
```

The workflow publishes `0.2.2` through OIDC and completes the trusted-publisher validation. The bootstrap `0.2.1` has no OIDC provenance; that is expected.

The workflow's version-exists check is only for idempotent reruns. It does not validate a new trusted publisher.

### Release process

```sh
# 1. Bump the version (choose patch/minor/major)
npm version patch --no-git-tag-version

# 2. Commit the version bump
git add package.json bun.lock
git commit -m "release: v0.2.2"
git push

# 3. Tag and push the tag
git tag v0.2.2
git push origin v0.2.2
```

The tag must match `package.json`:

- tag `v0.2.2` → version `0.2.2`

The workflow runs typecheck and tests, publishes with OIDC and automatic provenance, and creates a GitHub release.

You can also create the tag through the GitHub Releases UI. Make sure the tag starts with `v` and matches the package version.

### Verify

```sh
npm view @alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph version
npm view @alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph dist-tags
npm audit signatures
```

### Versioning and compatibility

- Use semver.
- Keep the plugin ID `flowgraph` stable; changing it changes the plugin storage namespace.
- Keep the RPC ID `flowgraph` stable.
- The current peer range is `@opencode/plugin >=2.0.32 <3`.
- A breaking RPC or workflow-schema change should be a major version.
- Prefer `npm deprecate` over unpublishing.

### Rollback

Publish a fixed patch version and deprecate the broken one:

```sh
npm deprecate @alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph@0.4.0 "Broken release; use 0.4.1"
```

Do not rewrite tags. The workflow publishes exactly the tagged commit.

### Troubleshooting

- **`ENEEDAUTH`**: the trusted publisher fields do not match the workflow exactly. Check repository, workflow filename, and `id-token: write`.
- **Provenance missing**: the repository must be public and the publish must use OIDC.
- **Configuration expired**: recreate the trusted publisher and publish within 2 days.
- **Wrong package version**: the tag and `package.json` version must match exactly.

# Workflow guide

This guide covers the two files you own: native OpenCode agents and the workflow YAML that connects them.

## Agent requirements

Agent nodes reference native OpenCode agent IDs from `.opencode/agents/*.md`. Agents must be:

- Not hidden
- `mode: primary` or `mode: all`
- Able to use tools, because every node reports through the `flowgraph_report` tool
- Given a `model`, or covered by a global `model` in `opencode.json(c)`

`mode: subagent` agents are rejected. The native contract runs subagents only through the `subagent` tool, and selecting one directly from a workflow would bypass that gate. Change the agent to `mode: all` if you want it in a workflow.

The plugin never creates, edits, or elevates agents.

```md
---
description: Reviews changes for correctness and missing tests
mode: primary
model: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash
permissions:
  - action: edit
    resource: "*"
    effect: deny
---

Review the change. Report findings in severity order.
```

## Workflow files

Workflows live in `.opencode/workflows/*.yaml`. The file stem must match `name`: `development.yaml` → `name: development`.

```yaml
version: 1
name: development
description: Development with iterative quality checks

entry: developer

limits:
  max_steps: 12
  timeout_seconds: 3600
  node_timeout_seconds: 900
  max_result_retries: 2
  max_recovery_attempts: 3
  max_repeat_transitions: 5

nodes:
  developer:
    agent: developer
    next: reviewer

  reviewer:
    agent: reviewer
    routes:
      approved: security
      changes_requested: developer
      blocked: pause

  security:
    agent: security
    routes:
      approved: complete
      changes_requested: developer
      blocked: pause
```

### Rules

- `version` must be `1`.
- `name` and every node ID are lowercase slugs.
- `entry` must be a node ID.
- An agent node defines exactly one of `next` or `routes`.
- `next` is unconditional.
- `routes` maps structured outcomes to targets.
- `complete` and `pause` are reserved terminal targets.
- Every node must be reachable from `entry`.
- Cycles are supported; `max_steps` and `max_repeat_transitions` bound them.
- Unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys, aliases, merge keys, custom tags, and oversized files are rejected.

### Parallel branches and workflow calls

A fork declares 2–16 distinct branch entry nodes and a join. The join is an agent node dedicated to that fork. It runs once after every branch reaches it and receives the last result from each branch in declaration order. Branches may contain routes, loops, and nested forks. Each branch has its own nodes until the join, and every branch node needs a path to the join.

A call references a workflow in the same repository by its YAML name. Map both child terminal outcomes, `complete` and `pause`, to caller targets. The child receives the parent's objective and recent results. Its final result passes back to the caller. Child steps, permissions, and failures are part of the same run.

```yaml
nodes:
  dispatch: { fork: [security, verification], join: integrate }
  security: { agent: security, next: integrate }
  verification:
    workflow: review
    routes: { complete: integrate, pause: investigate }
  investigate: { agent: reviewer, next: integrate }
  integrate: { agent: reviewer, next: complete }
```

The parent supplies the overall step, wall-clock, and recovery budgets. Each workflow supplies its own node timeout, report retry count, and repeated-transition limit. Forks and calls themselves consume no steps. The combined YAML sources must fit within 256 KiB, and workflow references must be acyclic.

Parallel branches and runs in the same checkout share files. Coordinate writes when agents can edit the same paths.

### Limits

`limits` and `max_steps` are required. Other limits have defaults.

| Limit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `max_steps` | required | Node executions, including repetitions |
| `timeout_seconds` | `3600` | Wall-clock run deadline |
| `node_timeout_seconds` | unset | Bound for one node; the runner interrupts its session on timeout |
| `max_result_retries` | `2` | Correction turns after a missing report |
| `max_recovery_attempts` | `3` | Restart reconciliation attempts |
| `max_repeat_transitions` | `5` | Stops a repeated transition sequence that makes no progress |

## Structured outcomes

V2 session prompts do not support a native response schema. The plugin registers a typed tool, `flowgraph_report`, which the node prompt asks the agent to call exactly once when finished:

```json
{
  "outcome": "changes_requested",
  "summary": "The implementation has an unhandled error path.",
  "feedback": "Handle the error and add a regression test.",
  "evidence": [
    { "kind": "file", "value": "src/example.ts:42" }
  ]
}
```

The plugin validates `outcome` against the current node's declared routes. Invalid outcomes are returned to the agent as tool errors. If a successful node never reports, the plugin sends a bounded correction prompt and then fails the node.

The orchestrator, not the agent, chooses the next node.

Evidence is **agent-reported**. It is stored separately from the native tool audit and is never presented as independently verified. The plugin does not claim a test passed because an agent said so.

The tool is registered for the whole location because OpenCode plugin tools are not session-scoped. Calls from normal, non-workflow sessions are rejected.

## Examples

Runnable examples live in [`examples/.opencode`](../examples/.opencode):

- `agents/` — developer, reviewer, security, tester, designer, and product owner agents
- `workflows/development.yaml` — development, review, and security loop
- `workflows/review.yaml` — a smaller two-stage review loop
- `workflows/product-delivery.yaml` — product, design, build, and review flow
- `workflows/parallel-review.yaml` — parallel security and review branches with a workflow call and a join

# Interfaces

The plugin exposes the same run model through four surfaces: RPC, the server `/flowgraph` command, the TUI, and the experimental Desktop GUI.

## RPC

The plugin registers the `flowgraph` RPC at each OpenCode location where it is loaded. The shared contract is exported from `@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph/rpc`.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/client"
import { FlowgraphRpc } from "@alvarolorentedev/opencode-flowgraph/rpc"

const client = OpenCode.make({ baseUrl, headers })
const workflows = client.rpc(FlowgraphRpc)
const location = { directory: "/workspace/project" }

const workflowsList = await workflows.listWorkflows(undefined, { location })

const started = await workflows.startRun(
  {
    workflowID: "development",
    objective: "Implement the requested change.",
    requestID: crypto.randomUUID(),
  },
  { location },
)

let detail = await workflows.getRun({ runID: started.runID }, { location })
while (detail.run.status === "running" || detail.run.status === "pausing") {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1_000))
  detail = await workflows.getRun({ runID: started.runID }, { location })
}

const unsubscribe = workflows.events.on("runUpdated", (event) => {
  if (event.location.directory !== location.directory) return
  console.log(event.data.runID, event.data.status, event.data.currentNode)
})
```

Events are live-only. After reconnecting, call `listRuns` or `getRun`.

### Methods

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `capabilities` | Plugin, RPC, schema, feature, and limit versions |
| `listWorkflows` | Discover project workflows and validation state |
| `getWorkflow` | Raw YAML, validated graph, agents, Mermaid |
| `validateWorkflow` | Validate YAML without writing |
| `saveWorkflow` | Create/update with a hash precondition |
| `deleteWorkflow` | Delete with a hash precondition |
| `startRun` | Start a run with an objective and idempotency key |
| `listRuns` | List project runs |
| `getRun` | Current state, step summaries, Mermaid, live permissions |
| `getRunGraph` | Structured graph, active steps, blockers, grouped child sessions, Mermaid mapping, controls |
| `getRunStep` | Full persisted step result |
| `pauseRun` | Safe pause between nodes |
| `resumeRun` | Resume, with explicit confirmation for ambiguous retries |
| `cancelRun` | Cancel future execution and interrupt active work |

Event: `runUpdated` with project, run, workflow, status, current node, revision, timestamp, and blocker. Events are live-only notifications; reconnecting clients must call `getRun` or `listRuns`.

Run details and graphs expose all active steps and blockers. The singular fields remain a primary view for existing callers. Step records from called workflows include `workflowID` and `callPath`.

All methods are location-scoped. The plugin rejects runs that belong to another project or canonical checkout. No `projectID` is accepted from the client.

### HTTP

The generic RPC route is:

```text
POST /api/rpc/flowgraph/{method}
```

The body is `{ "input": ... }`, and the response is `{ "output": ... }`. Pass `location[directory]` as a query parameter when the request is not already location-scoped.

### Errors

Declared errors include:

- `not_found`
- `invalid_input`
- `invalid_workflow`
- `unsafe_path`
- `stale_revision`
- `not_owner`
- `project_busy` (legacy)
- `idempotency_conflict`
- `too_many_runs`
- `permission_pending`
- `ambiguous_requires_confirmation`
- `not_resumable`
- `invalid_state`
- `unavailable`

Error data contains IDs, validation diagnostics, the current revision, or redacted permission summaries. It never contains prompts, objectives, YAML source, tool inputs, provider bodies, or credentials.

### Control semantics

- `pauseRun` sets `pausing` while admitted sessions drain, then sets `paused` with the remaining branches checkpointed.
- `resumeRun` requires the current `expectedRevision`.
- `resumeRun` returns `permission_pending` while a native permission request is outstanding.
- `resumeRun` requires `confirmRetry: true` to retry ambiguous steps. Other branches retain their checkpoints and live sessions.
- `cancelRun` marks the run cancelled and requests interruption of every outstanding session in that run.
- An idempotent retry with the same `requestID` returns the current run.
- `startRun` uses `requestID` plus the workflow/objective hash to detect conflicting retries.

## Server /flowgraph command

The server part registers a `flowgraph` slash command, so API-driven clients (mobile, web) that only see server commands via `command.list` can use the plugin without the TUI or Desktop GUI:

- `/flowgraph list` — list workflows
- `/flowgraph run <workflow-id> <objective...>` — start a run
- `/flowgraph runs` — list runs
- `/flowgraph graph <runID>` — describe one run

The command replies with plain text in the invoking session as a notice that does not resume the agent. It cannot open panels or dialogs; pause, resume, and cancel stay on RPC (`pauseRun`, `resumeRun`, `cancelRun`) and the TUI/GUI surfaces.

## TUI

The package ships a TUI part. It adds a full-screen `Workflow` page, a `Workflow graph` session panel, and a `/flowgraph` command.

### Open it

1. Run `/flowgraph` or use the command palette: **Workflow**.
2. If the current session belongs to a workflow run, the graph opens in its session panel.
3. Otherwise the full-screen workflow page opens. No session is required.

The page lists every workflow run visible on the connected server, including runs in other projects and worktrees. Select a run to see its structured graph.

### Commands

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `/flowgraph` or `/flowgraph graph` | Open the current workflow session panel, or the all-runs page. |
| `/flowgraph visuals` | Same as `graph`. |
| `/flowgraph runs` | Open the all-runs page. |
| `/flowgraph list` | List available workflows and start one. |
| `/flowgraph run <workflow-id> <objective...>` | Start a run. |
| `/flowgraph <workflow-id> <objective...>` | Shorthand for `run`. |

Starting a workflow asks for a missing workflow ID or objective with a dialog, then opens the new run's own session and graph panel.

### What it shows

- Every run on the server: workflow, status, directory, and objective.
- Workflow and run identity for the selected run.
- Status, revision, step count, blocker, and pending native permissions.
- A boxed top-down diagram: nodes are boxes, branches sit side by side, cycles route around a left-hand rail, long jumps around a right-hand rail, and rail edges enter boxes from the side.
- Outcome labels sit on their own row, or beside a vertical edge, so lines stay unbroken.
- Nodes with completed (green), active (yellow), failed or routed-back (red), paused, and pending markers and colours.
- Outcome-labelled edges, including cycles and terminal edges.
- Active nodes are highlighted. Called workflows show child progress under their call nodes.

The TUI does not render Mermaid. It renders the structured graph from `getRunGraph` directly. If the diagram does not fit the available width or height, the page falls back to a compact text list and says why.

### Keys

Workflow page:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `up` / `down` | Select a run |
| `o` | Open the selected run's session with its graph panel |
| `enter` | Open the primary active session |
| `s` | Pick any workflow session, grouped by graph node |
| `u` | Resume or retry ambiguous steps while siblings run |
| `p` | Pause or resume |
| `c` | Cancel the run |
| `r` | Refresh |

Session panel:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `enter` | Open the primary active session |
| `s` | Pick any workflow session, grouped by graph node |
| `u` | Resume or retry ambiguous steps while siblings run |
| `p` | Pause or resume |
| `c` | Cancel the run |
| `r` | Refresh |

The page and panel receive `runUpdated` events and refresh periodically as a fallback.

### Loading

The TUI part is exported as `./tui`. OpenCode loads it with the package's server part. For a TUI connected to a remote server, make sure the plugin is available in the TUI's plugin configuration as documented by OpenCode.

If no run appears, the page shows an explicit message. Runs are stored in the plugin storage of the server that started them; a TUI connected to a different server will not see another server's runs.

The page and panel also check the server plugin version through `capabilities`. If the TUI and server parts differ, they show a version-mismatch message instead of loading forever. Restart OpenCode after updating the plugin, and make sure the old `opencode-agent-workflows` package is removed from `opencode.json(c)` and `cli.json`.

## Desktop GUI

The package ships an experimental OpenCode Desktop GUI part, `./gui-experimental`.

### What it shows

- The generated Mermaid graph.
- Active nodes highlighted and child sessions grouped under their call nodes.
- Completed nodes styled green, nodes whose latest route looped back red until a later attempt passes, active nodes yellow, and failed/paused/pending nodes styled by state.
- Run status, revision, failure reason, blocker, and pending permission count.
- Click a node to open its native session. A node without a session shows a toast instead.
- Buttons for changing runs, pause, resume, cancel, and graph zoom.
- Live updates from `runUpdated`, with polling as a fallback.

### Multiple runs

Each workflow run has its own root session. Opening a run opens that session's tab and adds a graph panel to it, so several runs can stay open as separate graph tabs.

The **Workflow** command opens a run picker containing every run on the current server, across projects and worktrees. The **Runs** button in the graph panel reopens it. An unrelated session never silently shows another run's graph.

Runs are stored in the plugin storage of the server that started them. Desktop loads GUI parts from its own background server, so the TUI and Desktop must use the same server to see the same runs.

### Requirements

- OpenCode Desktop with the experimental GUI plugin API.
- The plugin must be configured in the **global** `opencode.json(c)` so Desktop can load the GUI bundle.
- The server part must load successfully. A plugin whose server part fails has no GUI.

### Build

The GUI entry must be one prebuilt CommonJS file:

```sh
bun run build:gui
```

This writes `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`. The release workflow and `prepublishOnly` build it automatically.

The Desktop GUI API is experimental and may change between OpenCode releases. The server RPC and TUI graph use the stable structured `getRunGraph` model, so changes to the GUI part do not affect the orchestrator.

## Mermaid

Mermaid is derived output, never an input or execution format. `renderMermaid(graph)` is a pure exported function; the RPC returns the same string. Output is deterministic, uses synthetic safe node IDs, and escapes labels. No `click`, `style`, or other executable directives are emitted.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    n0["Developer"]
    n1["Reviewer"]
    n2["Security"]
    complete["Complete"]
    pause["Pause"]
    n0 --> n1
    n1 -->|approved| n2
    n1 -->|changes_requested| n0
    n1 -->|blocked| pause
    n2 -->|approved| complete
    n2 -->|changes_requested| n0
    n2 -->|blocked| pause
```

# Operations and recovery

## Run lifecycle

Statuses: `running`, `pausing`, `paused`, `blocked`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

`blocked` means all remaining branches need a native permission decision or explicit retry. While a sibling can make progress, the run stays `running` and exposes the blocked step separately.

- Each run has a stable root session. Agent steps use fresh native child sessions, including steps from called workflows.
- Separate runs in the same checkout can execute concurrently. They share the files and can conflict if agents write the same paths.
- The root workflow and all referenced definitions and hashes are snapshotted at start. Native agents are resolved when each session starts, so changes to agent definitions affect later steps.
- A user pause drains admitted steps and preserves pending branches. A root terminal `pause` ends the run in a non-resumable state. A child's `pause` follows the caller's declared route.
- Cost and token usage are provider-reported estimates. Restart reconciliation protects workflow state, while external tool effects can still repeat after a confirmed retry.

## Execution model

The scheduler checkpoints the runnable branches, active sessions, pending joins, and call frames. Before prompting an agent, it reserves a step slot and records the session and prompt ID. The root budget applies across all branches and calls. Each completion records the step, then advances its branch and updates the join in one run checkpoint. Cancel, fatal failure, and timeout stop admission and request interrupts for that run's outstanding sessions.

## Storage

Runtime state lives in OpenCode plugin storage, keyed by project:

```text
v1/runs/<projectID>/<runID>
v1/steps/<projectID>/<runID>/<stepID>
v1/reports/<projectID>/<runID>/<stepID>
v1/run-sources/<projectID>/<runID>
v1/workflow-backups/<projectID>/<workflowID>/<hash>
v1/idem/<projectID>/<sha256(requestID)>
```

Workflow definitions remain YAML files in `.opencode/workflows`. Runtime checkpoints are never written into the repository.

Storage has no transactions or compare-and-swap. A host-local file lock protects ownership of each run. After an unclean shutdown, recovery retries busy run locks until they become available. In-process serialization protects run transitions, idempotent start admission, and the stored-run cap. Control RPCs require the current revision. Use one OpenCode server per project database.

## Restart and recovery

| Crash point | Recovery |
|---|---|
| Before prompt admission | Retry preparation when native session history is empty |
| Prompt admitted, node still active | Wait/reconcile; do not prompt again |
| Node succeeded and valid report exists | Persist the step and continue |
| Node succeeded but report is missing | Block with `missing_report`; require an explicit resume |
| Node failed or interrupted | Fail on native failure. Block the affected branch on interruption. |
| No terminal idle outcome | Block with `ambiguous_node` |
| Branch arrived at a join | Preserve the arrival and reconcile outstanding branches |
| Recovery attempts exhausted | Fail with `recovery_exhausted` |
| Run deadline expired | Fail with `run_timeout` |

Recovery preserves completed steps and join arrivals. A step that finished before the last checkpoint is reconciled from its saved result or native session and report. Existing sequential records are read in place and resume with one branch.

`resumeRun` with `confirmRetry: true` retries ambiguous steps in new sessions after their prior sessions are confirmed stopped. Resolve any pending native permissions before resuming.

Node sessions are child sessions of the workflow-run session. OpenCode's native restart sweep resumes top-level orphaned claims and releases orphaned child claims, so the workflow plugin owns node-session reconciliation.

## Failure boundaries

- Missing/invalid report after bounded corrections: node/run fails.
- Native failure or interruption: explicit failure or blocked state.
- Permission pending: blocked, never auto-approved.
- Ambiguous active node after restart: blocked, never automatically re-prompted.
- Storage corruption: invalid state, fail closed.
- Duplicate runners are excluded by the per-run ownership lock.

## Permissions and Git

- Native permissions are respected.
- Pending permission requests are surfaced through `getRun` and native sessions.
- The plugin never auto-approves a permission.
- The plugin adds no Git side effects: no branches, commits, pushes, pull requests, worktrees, or release process.
- Agents may use Git under their own native permissions and project policy.
- Background `subagent` and `shell` calls are rejected inside workflow sessions by default because they would outlive the agent step. Set the plugin option `allowBackgroundWork: true` to opt out.
- Workflow nodes cannot modify protected configuration paths: `.opencode`, `opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `AGENTS.md`, `.git`, and `.github`. File edits are blocked directly; destructive shell commands are blocked by a command-text guard. Reads remain allowed.
- Add project-specific protected paths with the plugin option `protectedPaths: ["infra", ".env"]`. The shell guard is heuristic; native permissions remain the security boundary.
- Workflow file writes are restricted to `.opencode/workflows`, reject symlinks/path traversal, use atomic replacement, and require the current content hash.
